title: Docs + terminal cross-surface scope-isolation & end-to-end verification (runs last)

background.reference: GitHub issue #307; mirrors epic_27's terminal verification story (US-27.17) pattern
background.includes: Every prior story asserts its own slice; this story proves the pillar end-to-end across app/api/mcp and writes the memory-vs-knowledge documentation. It depends on every leaf story and runs DEAD LAST.

priority_note: Terminal story: owns the epic-wide scope-isolation proof and the docs so no earlier story is blocked mid-loop on cross-surface concerns.

story.i_want_to: run one end-to-end pass that writes and recalls memory through every surface (context, API, MCP) and proves cross-tenant/cross-subject isolation holds everywhere, plus document the memory-vs-knowledge boundary
story.so_that: the agent-memory pillar ships proven and understandable, not just unit-green

rationale: Scope isolation is the security property of the whole subsystem; asserting it once per layer is not the same as asserting it holds across the full write→embed→recall→UI path. A single terminal verification (the epic_27 model) plus authoritative docs turns a set of merged stories into a trustworthy, teachable feature.

acceptance_criteria.description: docs/agent-memory.md written: the subsystem architecture, the two tiers (session vs long-term), the scope model, and an explicit 'when to use memory vs knowledge (vs the future context retriever)' section. It reconciles/absorbs any content the removed docs/cole-medin-self-evolving-wiki.md carried (that transcript is now KB hub fb9abd73).
README.md (feature + memory_* tool list), CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (agent guidance: pick memory_* vs knowledge_*), and CHANGELOG.md are updated. OpenAPI docs render the memory endpoints at /swaggerui.

An end-to-end test writes a memory via the API, drains embedding, recalls it via the context AND the API, and asserts the same memory is reachable through each — one coherent path, not three isolated stubs.

A cross-surface scope-isolation suite proves a memory written under (tenant T, subject A) is NOT retrievable as tenant U, nor as subject B of T, through the context, the API, and the MCP tool — closing the leak surface epic-wide.

A documented seam note for #308 (auto-promotion) and mkreyman/claude-config#85 (skills consumer): where the compiler hooks in (source='promoted', supersede) and which memory_* tools the skills call. No implementation of those here — just the verified extension points.

test_cases.name: End-to-end write(API) → recall(context+API) for one memory
preconditions: Authenticated agent key; deterministic embedding stub
steps: recall via Loopctl.Memory and via POST /api/v1/memory/recall
expected_results: Both recalls return the same memory; scores present

test_cases.name: Cross-tenant and cross-subject isolation holds on every surface
steps: Attempt recall/list/forget as tenant U and as (T, B) via context, API, and MCP
expected_results: Never returned or mutated on any surface; no existence leak

technical_notes: Model on epic_27's US-27.17 terminal-verification pattern: this story depends on all leaves and runs last so no implementation story blocks on cross-surface concerns.
Docs are authoritative for the three-layer mental model (knowledge / memory / context-retriever) that the Cole Medin comparison surfaced — keep it short and decision-oriented.
Do not implement #308 or #85 here; only assert and document the seams they rely on.
